title: Uptight — five open location questions
orderingNote: The ranking is a suggested research order: first close the two photographic gaps, then resolve business adjacency and connect the documented filming area to a still. It does not change any location’s confidence.

questions.title: Can we match the whole Madison Square facade?
questions.summary: The proposed identification is the Madison Square Building at 7812–14 Hough Avenue, at East 79th Street. The corner comparison is persuasive; the full central arch and balcony arrangement remain unmatched.

checked.text: Frame 63 shows MADISON roof lettering, heavy white corner blocks, stacked balconies and a tall central arch. The possible word SQUARE is less legible.
The Cleveland Landmarks Commission inventory names a Madison Square Building at 7812–14 Hough Avenue, built in 1915 and since demolished.
A 1964 Hough / East 79th photograph supplies the drugstore-corner comparison. A 1972 aerial gives site context. Neither resolves the complete arch and balcony pattern.
The 1943–44 and 1955 apartment-directory scans list Madison Square at 7820 Hough Avenue, while the municipal inventory uses 7812–14. The relationship between these address forms remains unresolved.

links.title: 1955 directory, Madison Square at 7820 Hough, printed p. 1662
1943–1944 directory, Madison Square at 7820 Hough, printed p. 1528

questions.missing: A dated full facade photograph or building drawing tied to the building’s address, showing the central arch and entire balcony pattern. A parcel, permit or building plan should also reconcile 7820 with 7812–14 Hough.
questions.closure: The full frontage should explain how the corner drugstore, arch, balconies and roof lettering fit one building. A conflicting facade is useful evidence as well.

questions.title: Is the final through-truss the former Clark Avenue Bridge?
questions.summary: Clark Avenue is the stronger candidate for the bridge beside the steelworks. The former West 3rd Street attribution has been withdrawn, and no exact replacement pin is asserted.

checked.text: Frame 658 shows a long road through-truss with dense overhead bracing. The tall structure in frame 654 is blast-furnace equipment, so it cannot support the old lift-bridge identification.

Michael A. Fuerst’s 1984 demolition photograph in the County Engineer collection provides a comparison for bridge form and the industrial setting. It is later than the 1968 film and does not reproduce the film’s road-level view.
A 1935 photograph taken from Clark Avenue documents neighboring Republic Steel furnaces. That establishes context rather than the film’s camera angle.

questions.missing: A dated road-level photograph of the former Clark Avenue crossing that can be compared with frame 658’s repeated portal shapes, overhead bracing, roadway and relationship to the furnaces.
questions.closure: A match should account for several fixed structural details in one view. If another crossing fits better, identify the same details and the source that establishes its location.

questions.title: Which Leader Drug branch stood beside the furniture sign?
questions.summary: The red FURNITURE KRO… sign may read Kronheim. The missing connection is a particular Leader Drug branch beside that furniture frontage during the filming period.

checked.text: Leader Drug appears in the street-speech sequence; frames 151 and 153 add the partly readable red furniture sign. The sign’s full name remains an inference.
A 1955 directory lists Kronheim retail at 2041 East 55th Street. The company history supports an earlier East 55th store, but these records do not establish the 1968 pharmacy pairing.
A 1960 photograph shows a Leader Drug branch at East 9th / St. Clair. Its facade was not a sufficiently convincing match to frame 169.

The Cleveland Press Photograph Collection finding aid lists separate Kronheim Furniture Co. and Leader Drug Stores folders in the Subjects series, PH2000.000PRE. The folder index does not give a specific image date, address or evidence that the shops were neighbors.

links.title: Cleveland Press Photograph Collection finding aid, printed p.29

questions.missing: A record near 1968 that places a Leader Drug branch next to the candidate furniture shop, together with a frontage photograph matching the pharmacy and its neighboring signs in the film.
questions.closure: An address or business name alone does not settle the branch. The adjacency and visible frontage should agree with the same block.

sources.title: Frame collection and original location hypotheses

questions.title: Can the hotel and blood-bank frontage be placed on one block?
questions.status: Open · hotel name and address unconfirmed
questions.summary: The script above the green HOTEL sign in frame 413 is read tentatively as Colonial. Cleveland’s Colonial Hotel at 527 Prospect Avenue is a comparison target; the name has not established the filming address.

checked.text: The reviewed sequence includes the projecting HOTEL sign, a restaurant, clearance-sale windows and BLOOD BANK / DONORS PAID neon. These neighboring frontages offer more useful checks than the tentative hotel name alone.
The Colonial Hotel record supplies the 527 Prospect Avenue name and address. The review has not matched its facade and neighboring shops to this sequence.
The separate Los Angeles theatre sequence does not locate this later hotel street. A cut between sequences is not proof of geographic continuity.

questions.missing: A dated streetscape or addressed property record that locates the hotel entrance and the adjoining blood bank or shops, with enough of the frontage visible to compare against frames 411–430.
questions.closure: The hotel, projecting sign and neighboring businesses should fit the same historical block. A different city or hotel remains possible until that match is made.

sources.title: Frame collection and original location hypotheses
Historic L.A. Theatres Appearing in Movies: Uptight

questions.title: Can one still be tied to East 86th Street and Wade Park Avenue?
questions.summary: A contemporary account places the production in this neighborhood. The open question is which, if any, of the indexed stills can be connected to a particular site there.

checked.text: Printed page 3 of the public FBI file records a June 5, 1968 source account of filming in the East 86 Street and Wade Park area, including a reported interruption at 9 p.m. on June 4.

The file includes an excerpt from the June 5 Cleveland Press article “Producer Sees Mayor After Film Interruption.” This supports investigating the production area without identifying a house, bowling alley or police-station frame.

questions.missing: A contemporaneous production photograph, location record or dated architectural image that ties a recognizable filmed exterior to an address in this area and matches a specific indexed still.
questions.closure: Keep the frame unassigned until the source-to-still connection is established. Neighborhood proximity and editing continuity do not supply that connection.
